title: Chemistry
description: CBSE Class XI Chemistry: nine official theory units from Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry to Hydrocarbons — 70 marks of theory plus 30 marks of practical work — taught with worked numericals, reaction reasoning and step-by-step mechanisms.

syllabusBaselines.source: CBSE, Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27, Secondary Curriculum Part 2 (Classes XI-XII), Chemistry subject code 043 (cbseacademic.nic.in/web_material/CurriculumMain27/SecPart2/Chemistry_SecP2_2026-27.pdf), downloaded and read in full (15 pages) in October 2026.
syllabusBaselines.note: Verified October 2026. The document carries 'CLASSES XI-XII (2026-27)' on its first page. Course structure Class XI: nine units totalling 70 marks — Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry 7, Structure of Atom 9, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties 6, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure 7, Chemical Thermodynamics 9, Equilibrium 7, Redox Reactions 4, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques 11, Hydrocarbons 10 — plus Practical 30 (Volumetric Analysis 8, Salt Analysis 8, Content Based Experiment 6, Project Work 4, Class record and viva 4). Two topics printed in the document (s & p Block Elements; The Gaseous State) are explicitly stated to be 'included in the syllabus but assessed only formatively'; they are registered in their own section labelled formative and are never presented as summatively examined material. Question paper design (Classes XI & XII): no chapter-wise weightage, no overall choice, 33% internal choice in all sections; domains weighted Remembering and Understanding 28 (40%), Applying 21 (30%), Analysing, Evaluating and Creating 21 (30%). Prescribed books: NCERT Chemistry Parts I and II for Class XI and the NCERT Manual of Microscale Chemistry laboratory kit, identified by title only. No chapter has been added beyond the topics printed in this document.

sections.title: Chemistry (Theory)
sections.description: Nine official units totalling 70 marks: Units 1-2 16, Units 3-4 13, Units 5-7 20, Units 8-9 21. Internal assessment and the practical examination carry the remaining 30 marks of the 100-mark subject.

groups.title: Unit 1: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry (7 marks)

chapters.title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
chapters.blurb: The importance of chemistry, nature of matter, measurement of properties, uncertainty in measurement, the laws of chemical combination, Dalton's atomic theory, atomic and molecular masses, the mole concept, percentage composition, and stoichiometric calculations.

chapters.title: Structure of Atom
chapters.blurb: Discovery of sub-atomic particles, the evolution of atomic models, the developments leading to Bohr's model and the Bohr model for hydrogen, the photoelectric effect and line spectra, and the quantum mechanical model of the atom with orbitals and quantum numbers.

groups.title: Unit 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties (6 marks)

chapters.title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
chapters.blurb: Why elements need classification, the genesis of periodic classification from Dobereiner to Moseley, the modern periodic law and the present form of the periodic table, nomenclature of elements with atomic number above 100, electronic configuration and the s-, p-, d- and f-blocks, and the periodic trends in properties of elements.

groups.title: Unit 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure (7 marks)

chapters.title: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure
chapters.blurb: The Kossel-Lewis approach, the ionic or electrovalent bond, bond parameters, the valence shell electron pair repulsion theory, valence bond theory, hybridisation, molecular orbital theory and bonding in homonuclear diatomic molecules, and hydrogen bonding.

chapters.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
chapters.blurb: Thermodynamic terms and state functions, the first law, measurement of delta U and delta H by calorimetry, enthalpy change and the enthalpies of different types of reactions, and spontaneity through Gibbs energy change and its relationship with equilibrium.

chapters.title: Equilibrium
chapters.blurb: Equilibrium in physical and chemical processes and dynamic equilibrium, the law of chemical equilibrium and the equilibrium constant, homogeneous and heterogeneous equilibria, the relationship between K, Q and Gibbs energy, Le Chatelier's principle, ionic equilibrium, acids bases and salts, the ionisation of acids and bases, buffer solutions and solubility equilibria of sparingly soluble salts.

chapters.title: Redox Reactions
chapters.blurb: The classical idea of oxidation and reduction, redox reactions in terms of electron transfer, the rules for assigning oxidation numbers, balancing redox reactions by the oxidation number and half-reaction methods, and redox reactions in terms of electrode processes.

groups.title: Unit 8: Organic Chemistry — Some Basic Principles and Techniques (11 marks)

chapters.title: Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques
chapters.blurb: A general introduction to organic chemistry, the tetravalence of carbon and the shapes of organic compounds, structural representations and classification of organic compounds, IUPAC nomenclature, isomerism, the fundamental concepts of organic reaction mechanisms including electron displacement effects, the purification of organic compounds, and the qualitative and quantitative analysis of organic compounds.

chapters.title: Hydrocarbons
chapters.blurb: The classification of hydrocarbons, alkanes with their conformations of ethane, alkenes with geometrical isomerism and the E-Z notation, alkynes, aromatic hydrocarbons with resonance and aromaticity, electrophilic substitution in benzene, and the carcinogenicity and toxicity of hydrocarbons.

sections.title: Formative Topics (not summatively assessed)
sections.paperLabel: CBSE Class XI · Formative assessment topics
sections.description: The official document includes s & p Block Elements and The Gaseous State in the syllabus but states they are assessed only formatively to reinforce understanding, without adding to summative assessments; schools may integrate them with existing chapters.

groups.title: Topics included in the syllabus but assessed formatively

chapters.title: s- and p-Block Elements
chapters.blurb: Formative only: electronic configuration, atomic and ionic radii, ionisation enthalpy, hydration enthalpy and the general trends in the physical and chemical properties of the s- and p-block elements across periods and down groups, including the unique behaviour of the first element of each group.

chapters.title: The Gaseous State
chapters.blurb: Formative only: a qualitative treatment of the gas laws, the ideal gas equation and the deviations of real gases from ideal behaviour.

sections.title: Practical (30 marks)
sections.description: Volumetric Analysis 8, Salt Analysis 8, Content Based Experiment 6, Project Work 4, Class record and viva 4 — assessed inside the school laboratory.

groups.title: Laboratory work and evaluation scheme (30 marks)

chapters.title: Practical Work
chapters.blurb: The 30-mark practical course: basic laboratory techniques, characterization and purification of chemical substances, experiments based on pH, chemical equilibrium, volumetric estimation, qualitative analysis of one anion and one cation, the detection of nitrogen, sulphur and chlorine in organic compounds, and the project work scheme.
